name: trace
description: Vertical agent-decision timeline. Each step is a thought, tool call, observation, or error — with optional duration and timestamp. Distinct from `<Task>` (in-flight progress) and `<ChainOfThought>` (structured ReAct trace) — Trace is a chronological audit log for post-hoc inspection.

props.name: steps
props.description: Array of `TraceStep` objects ({ id: string; kind: TraceStepKind; title: string; detail?: ReactNode; durationMs?: number; timestamp?: ReactNode }). `kind` is one of `"think"` / `"tool-call"` / `"observation"` / `"error"`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the timeline list. e.g. "Agent decision trace".

props.name: size
props.description: Indicator size — `"sm"` for tight inline traces, `"md"` for the default detailed view.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes on the root `<ol>`.

examples.title: Migration agent trace
examples.description: Mixed kinds — think, tool-call, observation, error.
examples.code:
<Trace
  ariaLabel="Migration agent trace"
  steps={[
    { id: "1", kind: "think", title: "Plan the migration", durationMs: 450 },
    { id: "2", kind: "tool-call", title: "read users.sql", durationMs: 120 },
    { id: "3", kind: "observation", title: "12 columns, 1.2M rows" },
    { id: "4", kind: "error", title: "ALTER failed: column already exists" },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: Compact inline trace
examples.description: Use `size="sm"` for a tight trace embedded inside a card.

examples.title: Per-step detail with timestamp
examples.description: Pass `timestamp` for absolute clock time and `detail` for a body line beneath the title.
examples.code:
<Trace
  ariaLabel="Today's agent activity"
  steps={[
    {
      id: "fetch",
      kind: "tool-call",
      title: "GET /api/users",
      detail: "200 OK · 1.2KB",
      timestamp: "14:30:02",
      durationMs: 240,
    },
  ]}
/>

ai.whenToUse: To show a chronological audit log of an agent's decisions — every think / tool-call / observation / error in order, with timing. Pair with `<ToolCall>` for richer per-step tool invocation rendering and `<Reasoning>` when a step's detail expands a thinking trace.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for in-flight task progress (use `<Task>`). Don't use for structured ReAct reasoning (use `<ChainOfThought>` — it enforces the thought/action/observation triple per step). Don't use as a generic activity feed for non-agent content (use `<Timeline>` from the components category).
commonMistakes: Using a `kind` value outside `"think"` / `"tool-call"` / `"observation"` / `"error"` — unknown kinds fall back to the error indicator visually but TS will reject the value at the type level
Putting agent reasoning prose in `step.title` — keep titles short imperative phrases; put the body in `step.detail` or compose `<Reasoning>` separately
Mixing user/assistant message turns into a Trace (Trace is the agent's internal log; conversational turns belong in `<MessageList>`)
Setting `durationMs` < 1 — render formats as `0ms` which is rarely useful; omit the prop instead when timing isn't measured
ai.accessibilityNotes: Renders a real `<ol>` with the consumer-supplied `ariaLabel` so screen readers announce it as an ordered list. Each step indicator has a kind-specific aria-label ("Thought", "Tool call", "Observation", "Error") so AT can voice the step kind without color cues. Step titles use semantic text — error-kind steps inherit `text-destructive` for visual emphasis but the kind label is the announced semantic.
